scope: Fourteen operational anomaly families plus multi-event correlation, the cross-signal composition pattern also present in the article. These fifteen overlapping navigation tags are not mutually exclusive statistical classes or validated detection coverage.

tags.label: Anomaly: Volumetric
tags.definition: Unusual total data or event volume relative to a relevant entity or workload baseline.
tags.exclude: File size, dataset size or attack volume mentioned without an analytical comparison.

tags.label: Anomaly: Frequency / Rate
tags.definition: Unexpected event frequency, repetition or rate within a defined window.
tags.exclude: An attack name such as brute force without rate, burst, threshold or detection analysis.

tags.label: Anomaly: Temporal
tags.definition: Unexpected timing, periodicity, intervals or activity relative to a temporal context.
tags.exclude: Publication dates, chronological incident narratives or ordinary scheduled operation alone.

tags.label: Anomaly: Peer Group
tags.definition: Behavior inconsistent with comparable roles, hosts, applications or cohorts.
tags.exclude: Any reference to a threat group, user role or industry without behavioral comparison.

tags.label: Anomaly: Sequence
tags.definition: Suspicious ordering or combination of related events, evaluated as a behavioral chain.
tags.exclude: Installation steps, course order, or a kill-chain list without detection or correlation analysis.

tags.label: Anomaly: Graph / Relationship
tags.definition: New or unusual entity-to-entity relationships, access paths or communication edges.
tags.exclude: A knowledge graph feature or threat-actor relationship without anomalous interaction analysis.

tags.label: Anomaly: Geographic / ASN
tags.definition: Unfamiliar source location or network context, including travel inconsistencies.
tags.exclude: Actor nationality, victim geography or an ASN IOC without source-history comparison.

tags.label: Anomaly: Identity / Access
tags.definition: Unexpected identity, token, factor, session, privilege or resource-access behavior.
tags.exclude: Routine IAM configuration, credential theft capability or authentication mechanics alone.

tags.label: Anomaly: Rare Process / Service
tags.definition: Uncommon or first-seen process/service behavior relative to host role or approved inventory.
tags.exclude: Any malware process or Windows service without rarity, inventory or contextual reasoning.

tags.label: Anomaly: Parent–Child Execution
tags.definition: Suspicious process ancestry or child execution evaluated in its host/application context.
tags.exclude: Generic process-creation API descriptions without lineage or defensive interpretation.

tags.label: Anomaly: Data Movement
tags.definition: Unexpected transfer, export, destination or data-access flow with defensive interpretation.
tags.exclude: Exfiltration as a tactic name or authorized data migration without transfer analysis.

tags.label: Anomaly: Protocol / Application
tags.definition: Protocol or application use inconsistent with expected structure, destination or purpose.
tags.exclude: Normal HTTP, DNS or application setup without behavioral or protocol-abuse analysis.

tags.label: Anomaly: Negative / Absence
tags.definition: Unexpected disappearance of expected telemetry, heartbeats or activity.
tags.exclude: A generic logging gap, missing data, or a tool-disable event without expected-stream reasoning.

tags.label: Anomaly: State Change
tags.definition: Unexpected changes to accounts, permissions, configuration, services or resources.
tags.exclude: Normal setup instructions or a change event with no security/detection context.

tags.label: Anomaly: Multi-Event Correlation
tags.definition: Multiple weak signals linked by entity and time to evaluate a suspicious behavioral chain. This is a composition pattern, not an independent statistical family.
tags.exclude: Generic enrichment, several unlinked alerts, a product correlation feature or a chronological narrative alone.
